summary: Iron Mountain state tower planned in 1932, with road work to a site on Pewabic Hill; a 1954 survey station (Fox RM 1) describes a 120 ft steel structure. Whether that station is on Millie Hill is unconfirmed, and no source says what remains today.

facts.design: Steel structure on four legs with a concrete foundation

access.note: A neighborhood website describes trails and a summit reached from Tower Drive. It does not say who owns the summit.

visit.trail_note: The Millie Hill neighborhood site describes trails and a summit reached from Tower Drive.

events.note: State announced a 102 ft fire tower for Iron Mountain in August; road work to a site on Pewabic Hill began in September. Completion is not confirmed.
Newspaper item (Oct 7, 1953) mentions the fire tower on Pewabic Hill, where antenna tests were under way.
Coast and Geodetic Survey describes the Fox RM 1 station as steel, on four legs, about 120 ft high.

evidence.supports: Station is a steel structure, about 120 ft high, with four legs on a concrete foundation
evidence.quote: EAST OF THE MAIN STREET IN IRON MOUNTAIN. IT IS OF STEEL

evidence.supports: Station stands on a timbered hill about 1.3 miles east of Main Street
evidence.quote: STATION IS LOCATED ON A HIGH TIMBERED HILL ABOUT 1.3 MILES

evidence.supports: Four legs on a concrete foundation
evidence.quote: HAS FOUR LEGS SET ON A CONCRETE FOUNDATION, AND
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1954 (DAJ)

evidence.supports: Survey point is designated Fox RM 1
State conservation department announced plans in August 1932 for a fire tower at Iron Mountain
evidence.quote: The state conservation department has made plans for the erection in Iron Mountain of a fire tower as part of its program of increasing the number of posts from which forest and brush fires may be detected.

evidence.supports: Planned tower was 102 feet tall, probably at the top of Iron Mountain
evidence.quote: It will be of standard height, 102 feet, and will probably be located at the top of Iron Mountain, which is at the head of East Ludington street.

evidence.supports: September 1932 road work to the tower site on Pewabic Hill
evidence.quote: Work on the construction of an automobile road to the site of the fire tower to be erected on a high point east of the old Walpole mine, on Pewabic Hill, is underway

evidence.supports: October 1953 item mentions the fire tower on Pewabic Hill, where antenna tests were under way
evidence.quote: Preliminary tests for a community antennae, a new development designed to bring clearer reception to television viewers in fringe areas, is underway on Pewabic Hill, near the fire tower

evidence.supports: State Department of Conservation is the agency named on the Iron Mountain page
Published coordinates for the Millie Hill summit (the survey page gives none for the station)
Summit is reached from Tower Drive and has panoramic views over Iron Mountain
evidence.quote: The summit of Millie Hill (476 meters elevation) accessible from Tower Drive provides serene panoramic views over Iron Mountain

evidence.supports: The hill has winding trails and scenic lookout points
evidence.quote: winding trails, scenic lookout points, and the fascinating Millie Mine bat cave

corrections.why: A survey data sheet is a source, not the agency that ran a tower. The 1932 coverage names the state conservation department as planning the Iron Mountain tower. Whether that tower is this station is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1932 plan gave 102 ft and the 1954 survey gives about 120 ft. The record keeps 36.6 m from the survey, which describes a standing structure. The sources do not say the 1932 tower was built to plan.

notes_for_editor: Identity: the survey page gives no coordinates for Fox RM 1, so the station cannot be matched to the Millie Hill summit (MountainZone lists 45.820789, -88.0442934 for the summit). The 1932 and 1953 newspaper items name Pewabic Hill, and no source links the two names. The Iron Mountain page's 1922 steel tower entry does not name a hill, so it is left out. The agency 'NGS Data Sheet' is a source, hence the correction. Nothing after 1954 was found, and no staffing record. The Travel the Mitten and Tripadvisor pages could not be fetched.
